# Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2010: "A Future Fair for All"

## Context and Vision
The 2010 Labour manifesto was launched during a period of significant crisis – British troops were fighting in Afghanistan, the global economy was recovering from the 2008 financial crisis, and the parliamentary expenses scandal had severely damaged public trust in politics. Labour positioned this as a programme for national renewal, based on fairness, respect, decency and openness.

## Economic Recovery
Labour's central economic argument was against cutting public spending prematurely. They committed to halving the deficit over four years through economic growth, fair taxation (including the new 50p top rate and bonus taxes on bankers), and targeted spending cuts to lower priorities. They pledged to reform banking through tighter regulation, support for small businesses through a £4 billion UK Finance for Growth Fund, and infrastructure investment including High Speed Rail and universal broadband.

## Public Services
The manifesto promised to protect frontline spending on the NHS, schools, childcare and policing. Key commitments included legally binding NHS patient guarantees, free nursery provision, a "3Rs Guarantee" for struggling primary pupils, and maintaining record police numbers. They proposed reforms giving patients more choice and enabling successful schools to take over failing ones.

## Social Policy
Labour pledged to end long-term unemployment through job guarantees, raise the minimum wage in line with earnings, expand apprenticeships, and help first-time buyers through stamp duty exemptions. They proposed a new National Care Service offering free home care for those with greatest needs and protection from catastrophic residential care costs.

## Immigration and Security
The manifesto supported an Australian-style points-based immigration system, ensuring economic needs are met while controlling numbers. They pledged to maintain police resources, expand CCTV and DNA databases, and take tougher action on anti-social behaviour.

## Political Reform
Responding to the expenses scandal, Labour proposed referenda on electoral reform (Alternative Vote) and an elected House of Lords, fixed-term parliaments, a statutory lobbyist register, and potentially lowering the voting age to 16.

## International Affairs
Labour reaffirmed commitment to Afghanistan, maintaining the nuclear deterrent, active EU engagement, and meeting the 0.7% aid target. They advocated for reform of global institutions including the UN, IMF and G20.
